issues.description: PaymentDetails interface stores sensitive payment card data (cardNumber, cvv) in plain text. This violates PCI DSS compliance requirements. If this data is logged, stored in memory dumps, or transmitted without encryption, it creates a critical security vulnerability.
issues.suggestion: Never handle raw card data in your application. Use a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, PayPal) that provides tokenization. Replace PaymentDetails with a payment token: { paymentToken: string; amount: number; }. Let the payment gateway handle sensitive card details.

issues.description: The processPremiumPayment function accepts and processes raw credit card details (cardNumber, cvv, expiryDate) directly. This makes your application subject to PCI DSS Level 1 compliance requirements, which is extremely costly and complex. Any logging, error handling, or data breach could expose this sensitive data.
issues.suggestion: Refactor to use a payment service provider's SDK (e.g., Stripe). Example: const paymentIntent = await stripe.paymentIntents.create({ amount, currency: 'usd', payment_method: paymentMethodId }); This keeps card data off your servers entirely.

issues.description: The chargeCard function logs payment errors to console.error, which may include the full payment object containing cardNumber, cvv, and other sensitive PCI data. This violates PCI DSS requirement 3.2 (never store sensitive authentication data after authorization).
issues.suggestion: Remove sensitive data before logging: console.error('Payment failed:', { lastFour: payment.cardNumber.slice(-4), amount, error: error.message }); Better yet, use a structured logger that automatically redacts sensitive fields.

issues.description: validatePaymentDetails only checks card number length is 16, but this excludes valid 13-15 digit cards (Visa, Amex). More critically, it performs NO Luhn algorithm validation, allowing completely fake card numbers through (e.g., '1111111111111111').
issues.suggestion: Implement proper Luhn checksum validation. However, the better solution is to not validate cards client-side at all—delegate to a PCI-compliant payment processor that handles validation securely.

issues.description: Expiry date validation uses 'new Date(2000 + parseInt(year))' which will break in 2100 (though unlikely to matter). More critically, the comparison 'expiryDateObj < new Date()' checks year-month but ignores that cards are valid through the last day of the expiry month, not the first day.
issues.suggestion: Fix the end-of-month logic: const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0, 23, 59, 59); // Last day of month at end of day. Also consider using a modern date library like date-fns for clarity.

issues.description: calculateSubscriptionPrice has hardcoded tax rate (8%) and processing fee (2.9%). Tax rates vary by jurisdiction and can change over time. Processing fees vary by payment provider and payment method.
issues.suggestion: Move pricing configuration to a database or config file that can be updated without code changes: const config = await getPricingConfig(userLocation); const tax = basePrice * config.taxRate; Return configuration by user's billing address to apply correct tax rates.

issues.description: chargeCard function simulates a payment gateway but provides no actual payment processing, idempotency, or fraud detection. In production, this would allow users to gain premium access without actually being charged, or be charged multiple times for the same subscription.
issues.suggestion: Integrate a real payment gateway with proper error handling and idempotency: const charge = await stripe.charges.create({ amount: Math.round(amount * 100), currency: 'usd', source: paymentToken, idempotency_key: `${userId}-${tier}-${Date.now()}` }); Include webhook handling for async payment confirmations.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription use JSON.parse(subscription.features) without error handling. If the database contains malformed JSON (corrupted data, manual edits), this will throw an unhandled exception and crash the request.
issues.suggestion: Add defensive parsing with fallback: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return features.includes(feature); } catch (error) { logger.error('Invalid features JSON for user', { userId, error }); return false; }

issues.description: The subscription expiry check uses 'validUntil < new Date()' which means a subscription expires at the very start of the expiry date. Users expect their subscription to be valid through the entire last day (until 23:59:59).
issues.suggestion: Adjust the comparison to be inclusive of the expiry date: const validUntil = new Date(subscription.valid_until); validUntil.setHours(23, 59, 59, 999); if (validUntil < new Date()) { return false; }

issues.description: upgradeUserSubscription sets validUntil to exactly 1 year from now using setFullYear. This doesn't account for leap years or the fact that billing cycles should typically start from the purchase date, not the current moment. If called multiple times rapidly, dates will differ.
issues.suggestion: Use a more explicit date calculation that's deterministic: const validUntil = new Date(new Date().setFullYear(new Date().getFullYear() + 1)); Or better, calculate from a billing cycle start date: const validUntil = addYears(billingCycleStart, 1);

issues.description: No rate limiting or fraud detection is implemented for payment processing. An attacker could attempt unlimited payment submissions, test stolen cards, or overwhelm the payment system with requests.
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting per user/IP: Use express-rate-limit or similar middleware to limit payment attempts to 3-5 per hour per user. Add CAPTCHA for suspicious patterns. Log and alert on multiple failed payment attempts.

issues.description: No audit logging exists for payment transactions. In case of disputes, fraud, or security incidents, there's no record of who attempted payments, when, or what the outcomes were. This is required for PCI DSS compliance and fraud investigation.
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive audit logging: await auditLog.create({ event: 'payment_attempt', userId, tier, amount, success: paymentSuccessful, ip: req.ip, timestamp: new Date(), lastFour: payment.cardNumber.slice(-4) }); Store securely with tamper-proof logging.

issues.description: The module has no authorization checks to verify that the userId making the payment is actually the authenticated user. An attacker could potentially upgrade another user's account or manipulate user IDs.
issues.suggestion: Add authorization validation at the start of processPremiumPayment: if (authenticatedUserId !== userId) { throw new AuthorizationError('Cannot process payment for another user'); } Pass authenticatedUserId from the session/JWT token.

issues.description: If chargeCard succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription fails (database error, network issue), the user is charged but doesn't receive premium access. There's no rollback, refund logic, or retry mechanism for this partial failure scenario.
issues.suggestion: Wrap in a transaction or implement compensating actions: try { const paymentId = await chargeCard(payment, amount); await upgradeUserSubscription(userId, tier, paymentId); } catch (error) { await refundPayment(paymentId); throw error; } Or use a payment processor with webhooks for eventual consistency.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription make separate database queries that could be combined. If checking multiple features for the same user, this results in redundant queries.
issues.suggestion: Cache subscription data per request: const subscription = await getUserSubscription(userId); if (!subscription || subscription.validUntil < new Date()) return false; return subscription.features.includes(feature); Or implement application-level caching with a short TTL.

issues.description: Feature lists for premium and enterprise tiers are hardcoded in upgradeUserSubscription. Adding or changing features requires code changes and deployment. This makes A/B testing or dynamic feature rollouts impossible.
issues.suggestion: Move feature definitions to a database or configuration: const tierConfig = await getTierConfig(tier); const features = tierConfig.features; This allows business users to modify features without developer intervention.

issues.description: The payment.amount is compared to the calculated amount, but there's no tolerance for floating-point rounding errors. If the client calculates 10.87999999 and the server calculates 10.88, the payment could be rejected.
issues.suggestion: Use a small epsilon for comparison or work in cents (integers): const amountInCents = Math.round(amount * 100); const paymentInCents = Math.round(payment.amount * 100); if (paymentInCents < amountInCents) { throw new Error('Insufficient payment'); }

issues.description: The comments throughout the file mention 'NO TESTS' for critical payment and business logic. While this doesn't affect the code's runtime behavior, it significantly increases the risk of bugs being introduced during refactoring or feature additions.
issues.suggestion: Implement comprehensive unit tests for all payment logic, especially: validatePaymentDetails, calculateSubscriptionPrice, edge cases in date validation, and mock database interactions for subscription management.

codeQuality.summary: This file contains critical security vulnerabilities related to PCI DSS compliance, including handling raw credit card data, logging sensitive information, and lack of proper payment processing. Multiple high-severity issues exist around missing authorization, audit logging, transaction safety, and business logic bugs in date handling and feature validation. The code requires major refactoring to use a PCI-compliant payment processor and implement proper security controls.

testCoverage.summary: No tests exist for src/premium.ts. This file contains critical payment processing, card validation, pricing calculations, and authorization logic. All 5 exported functions and 3 private functions are completely untested, representing significant financial and security risk due to PCI-DSS violations (storing raw card data), missing input validation, and unverified business logic.

suggestions.description: Extract pricing configuration into a structured pricing strategy with constants at module level. Current implementation hardcodes pricing logic inside the function, making it hard to test, modify, or extend with new tiers.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes pricing configuration for easier testing and modification. Makes tax and fee rates visible at module level. Enables easy mocking of pricing in tests. More maintainable when adding new tiers or changing rates.

suggestions.description: Break down monolithic validation function into separate, focused validators. Current 29-line function does four distinct validations, making it hard to test individual rules and understand failure reasons.
suggestions.benefits: Each validation rule is independently testable and reusable. Validation logic reads declaratively. Easy to add specific error messages later. Functions follow single responsibility principle.

suggestions.description: Extract feature sets into a configuration map and create a dedicated function for calculating subscription validity period. Current implementation uses inline ternary and duplicates feature lists.
suggestions.benefits: Feature configuration is centralized and type-safe. Date calculation is reusable and testable. Eliminates conditional logic in favor of data-driven approach. Makes adding new tiers simpler.

suggestions.description: Use early returns to reduce nesting and simplify conditional flow. Current implementation has unnecessary nesting after the initial check.
suggestions.benefits: Reduces visual complexity and indentation depth. Makes the guard conditions more prominent. Added type annotation for parsed features improves type safety.

suggestions.description: Extract repeated subscription expiry check into a dedicated utility function. Both functions check if subscription is expired using the same logic.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes expiry logic for consistency. Makes the business rule explicit and testable. Improves readability with semantic naming. Makes it easy to change expiry logic globally.

suggestions.description: Use modern date arithmetic with explicit typing instead of magic number addition for year calculation.
suggestions.before:
const [month, year] = expiryDate.split('/');
const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month) - 1);
suggestions.benefits: Removes magic number. Adds radix parameter to parseInt for explicit base-10 parsing. Makes century assumption clear and configurable.

suggestions.description: Extract database queries into a repository pattern or query constants. SQL strings are scattered throughout functions, making them hard to test and maintain.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes SQL for easier review and modification. Enables query reuse and consistency. Makes functions more focused on business logic. Facilitates database abstraction and testing.

suggestions.description: Use early return pattern and add type annotation to parsed features for consistency.
suggestions.benefits: Consistent with hasFeatureAccess pattern. Adds type safety to JSON parsing. Reduces indentation.

refactorings.summary: The file has significant refactoring opportunities focused on extracting configuration data (pricing, features, queries) to module level, breaking down complex validation into focused functions, and applying consistent patterns for database access and expiry checking. These changes will improve testability, maintainability, and make the business logic more explicit.

recommendations.description: IMMEDIATE: Replace raw credit card handling with a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, PayPal, Square). Current implementation violates PCI DSS requirements by storing/processing sensitive card data (cardNumber, cvv) directly. This exposes the application to massive compliance costs, legal liability, and security breaches.

Write comprehensive unit tests for all payment processing functions (processPremiumPayment, validatePaymentDetails, chargeCard, calculateSubscriptionPrice). Zero test coverage on critical financial logic poses direct revenue and security risk. Focus on edge cases for insufficient amounts, invalid cards, and payment failures.

Remove sensitive data from error logging. The chargeCard function logs payment errors that may contain full card details. Implement structured logging with automatic PII redaction or only log non-sensitive fields (lastFour, amount, error message).

Implement rate limiting and fraud detection for payment endpoints. Add middleware to limit payment attempts to 3-5 per hour per user/IP. Log and alert on multiple failed attempts. Consider CAPTCHA for suspicious patterns.

Add comprehensive audit logging for all payment transactions. Record userId, tier, amount, success/failure, IP address, timestamp, and last four digits of card. Store in tamper-proof audit log for compliance and fraud investigation.

Create tests for authorization logic (hasFeatureAccess, getUserSubscription) covering: users without subscriptions, expired subscriptions, feature tier mismatches, and malformed JSON in database. These functions control access to paid features.

Fix card expiry validation to include the full last day of expiry month (23:59:59). Current logic expires cards at 00:00:00 on expiry date. Apply same fix to subscription expiry check in hasFeatureAccess.

Refactor validatePaymentDetails into separate focused functions (isValidCardNumber, isValidCvv, isValidExpiryFormat, isCardExpired). This improves testability and makes validation rules independently verifiable. Also add Luhn algorithm validation for card numbers.

Extract pricing configuration (basePrices, taxRate, processingFeeRate) and feature sets (TIER_FEATURES) to module-level constants. Extract SQL queries into a QUERIES object. This centralizes configuration, improves testability, and makes business rules more visible.

Add authorization checks to verify the authenticated user matches the userId parameter in processPremiumPayment. Without this, an attacker could potentially upgrade other users' accounts or manipulate user IDs.

Implement transaction handling or compensating actions to handle partial failures. If chargeCard succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription fails, the user is charged without receiving access. Add refund logic or use payment processor webhooks for eventual consistency.

Add defensive error handling for JSON.parse operations in hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription. Malformed JSON in the database will crash requests. Wrap in try-catch with fallback values and error logging.

Move tax rates and processing fees to a configuration system that accounts for user location and payment method. Current hardcoded 8% tax rate won't work for multi-jurisdiction compliance. Consider using a tax calculation API.

Move feature definitions for tiers to a database or configuration file. Currently hardcoded in upgradeUserSubscription, requiring code deployment to modify features. This prevents dynamic feature rollouts and A/B testing.
Implement caching for subscription data to reduce redundant database queries when checking multiple features for the same user. Use application-level cache with short TTL or per-request caching.
